title: Remark
body_md: Alternatively, it is possible to train a joint encoder $h_\theta(\hat{e} \mid V)$ that maps directly from perceptual observations to semantic encodings (i.e., logic clauses).

title: Definition
body_md:
For a configuration $i$, let $\delta_{i,P},\delta'_{i,P}\in\{\pm1\}$ for all $P\in\mathbf{P}$\footnote{For monadic predicates, each predicate $P$ appears in the formulation of Q-sentence as $\delta_{i,P}P(x_1)$ by itself.}. For $x_1,x_2\in\mathbf{X}$,
\[
Q_i(x_1,x_2)
=\bigwedge_{P\in\mathbf{P}}
\left(\delta_{i,P}P(x_1,x_2)\,\land\,\delta'_{i,P}P(x_2,x_1)\right),
\]
where $\delta_{i,P}=+1$ denotes $P(x_1,x_2)$ and $\delta_{i,P}=-1$ denotes $\neg P(x_1,x_2)$; similarly for $\delta'_{i,P}$. Each configuration $i$ therefore specifies one complete enumeration of predicate occurrences.
head: environment
name: Q-sentence

title: Definition
body_md:
Let $\mathbf{Q}$ denote all Q-sentences. For $\delta_{j,Q}\in\{\pm1\}$,
\[
C_j(x_1)
=\bigwedge_{Q\in\mathbf{Q}}
\delta_{j,Q}\big((\exists x_2)\,Q(x_1,x_2)\big),
\]
where $\delta_{j,Q}=+1$ asserts $(\exists x_2)Q(x_1,x_2)$ and $\delta_{j,Q}=-1$ asserts its negation.
head: environment
name: Attributive Constituent

title: Definition
body_md:
Let $\mathbf{C}_\mathbf{A}$ be the set of all attributive constituents. For $\delta_{k,C_A}\in\{\pm1\}$,
\[
C^{w,k}
=\bigwedge_{C_A\in\mathbf{C}_\mathbf{A}}
\delta_{k,C_A}\big((\exists x_1)C_A(x_1)\big),
\]
where the width $w$ is the number of conjuncts with $\delta_{k,C_A}=+1$. Here $\delta_{k,C_A}=+1$ asserts that some $x_1$ satisfies $C_A(x_1)$; $\delta_{k,C_A}=-1$ asserts that none do.
head: environment
name: Constituent

label: dnfinfol
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{dnfinfol}
Let $\mathcal{L}$ have finite dyadic predicates $\mathbf{P}$, and let $\mathcal{C}$ denote all constituents. For any closed general sentence $\varphi$,
\[
\varphi\equiv
\bigvee_{\substack{C^{w,k}\in\mathcal{C}\\ C^{w,k}\models\varphi}}
C^{w,k}.
\]
head: environment
name: Distributive Normal Forms in FOL

title: Remark
body_md: To seperate them from statistical probabilities, notation $c(\cdot)$ is used to denote inductive probabilities.
head: environment

label: degofconf
title: Definition
body_md:
\label{degofconf}
For any FOL expression $\varphi$ and evidence $e$, the \emph{conditional inductive logical probability} (degree of confirmation) of $\varphi$ given $e$ is
\[
c(\varphi \mid e)
= \frac{c(\varphi \land e)}{c(e)}.
\]
head: environment
name: Degree of Confirmation

label: cont-info
title: Definition
body_md:
\label{cont-info}
For any hypotheses $\varphi$, its content-information is
\[
\mathrm{cont}(\varphi)=1-c(\varphi).
\]
Given a fixed hypothesis $\varphi$ and evidence $e$, the conditional content information of evidence $e$ with respect to $\varphi$ is measured as:
\[
\mathrm{cont}(\varphi \mid e) = \mathrm{cont}(\varphi \land e) - \mathrm{cont}(e),
\]
head: environment
name: Content Information

title: Remark
body_md: These labels are conventional: any FOL sentences or sets of sentences may occupy these roles, with degree of confirmation measuring how strongly the evidence supports the hypothesis. In logical probability, all available evidence is represented by a single sentence $e$, formed by conjoining individual observations. Carnap \cite{carnap_logical_1962} explicitly separates methodological considerations---such as measurement procedures and noisy observations---from logical probability. Evidence is therefore not a statistical random variable, but an FOL observation report. Consequently, in defining types of information below, we do not take an expectation or average over the evidence. Hypotheses, initially uncertain, correspond to the possible FOL descriptions of an unknown. Once the true hypothesis is identified, it becomes part of the evidence.

title: Definition
body_md:
For each subset of constituents $\mathcal{C}_m \subseteq \mathcal{C}$ induced by $L_{\mathcal{T}}$, define the corresponding goal-oriented state as
\[
\varphi_m \equiv \bigvee_{C^{w,k} \in \mathcal{C}_m} C^{w,k}.
\]
The collection $\Phi = \{\varphi_1, \dots, \varphi_M\}$ is called the \emph{goal-state space}. Each goal state $\varphi_m \in \Phi$ is associated with a corresponding action $a_m$ from an action set $\mathcal{A} = \{a_1, \dots, a_R\}$.
head: environment
name: Goal-Oriented States

title: Definition
body_md:
Given evidence $e$, the inductive probability of a goal state $\varphi_m$ is
\[
c(\varphi_m \mid e) = \sum_{C^{w,k} \models \varphi_m} c(C^{w,k} \mid e).
\]
head: environment
name: Goal-Oriented Inductive Probability

title: Remark
body_md: Although each goal state $\varphi_m$ admits a constituent decomposition via Theorem~\ref{dnfinfol}, i.e., $\varphi_m \equiv \bigvee_{C^{w,k} \models \varphi_m} C^{w,k}$, in practice the goal states are grounded with respect to a specific ego vehicle. This is because we are typically not interested in the information that evidence conveys, on average, about the truth of a hypothesis for every vehicle---as the universal quantification in~(\ref{equ:rule1}) would suggest---but rather in evaluating the truth of each hypothesis with respect to a particular ego vehicle of interest.

title: Remark
body_md: Specifying $p(Q_i \mid \mathrm{Ct}_j)$ requires a sampling semantics (e.g., sampling a random pair, or an ego individual and then a partner). An attributive constituent $\mathrm{Ct}_j(x)$ specifies which Q-sentences are existentially realised for an individual, but not a probability distribution over them. Without an explicit sampling story, the transition $\mathrm{Ct}_j \to Q_i$ is logically meaningful but probabilistically incomplete.

title: Remark
body_md: The quantities $q_{hk}$ function as local support sizes. Q-relations that are logically impossible under a given $(C^w, D_\nu)$ are structural zeros---assigned probability exactly zero by the model, not merely unobserved. This makes Hilpinen's framework a constrained multinomial model where logic determines which categories are allowed and statistics determines how probable the allowed categories are.
